summary: The government's UAP disclosure machinery shifted into a higher gear this week with the establishment of a new interagency governance board tasked with coordinating investigations and declassification efforts across federal agencies. Alongside that structural change, a science advisory council formed to help crack what officials are calling "the UAP mystery," signaling a pivot toward bringing independent scientific expertise into what has historically been a classified intelligence domain. The Pentagon released its third batch of files through the PURSUE initiative, and newly declassified documents suggest China and Russia may have recovered anomalous objects, raising geopolitical stakes around the issue. Meanwhile, debate continues over source credibility and historical claims: investigators are still examining whether the so-called Majestic 12 papers are authentic, while a Vatican archives search turned up nothing despite earlier whistleblower claims. The FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act briefing deadline looms at the end of the month, so expect Congress to demand concrete updates on what these newly empowered bodies have actually found.
